title: Quinoa vs. Couscous: Nutrition Compared

seo.title: Quinoa vs. Couscous: Nutrition Compared
seo.meta_description: Per 100 g cooked, quinoa has about 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, and 2.8 g fiber; couscous about 112 calories, 3.8 g protein, and 1.4 g fiber.
seo.search_intent: Compare quinoa and couscous for calories, protein, fiber, gluten, and cooking use.

excerpt: Cooked quinoa and couscous are close in calories, but quinoa usually provides slightly more protein and about twice the fiber. Quinoa is naturally gluten-free, while traditional couscous is made from wheat semolina and contains gluten.
content_html:
They can fill the same space on a plate, but they are made from very different ingredients. Quinoa is a pseudocereal seed; couscous is a pasta-like product usually made from durum-wheat semolina.

Per 100 g cooked

USDA reference values put cooked quinoa around 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, and 2.8 g fiber per 100 g. Cooked couscous is around 112 calories, 3.8 g protein, and 1.4 g fiber.

The calorie difference is small. Quinoa has a modest protein edge and roughly double the fiber.

Gluten is a major difference

Quinoa is naturally gluten-free. Traditional couscous is made from wheat and contains gluten.

Micronutrients

Quinoa generally provides more magnesium and iron than refined couscous. Whole-wheat couscous can narrow some of the fiber and mineral gap.

In the kitchen

Couscous is faster, with many products hydrating in minutes. Quinoa usually takes about 15 minutes and keeps a firmer texture.

Choose couscous for speed; quinoa for more fiber, a different amino-acid profile, and natural gluten-free status.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Cooked quinoa usually has slightly more: about 4.4 g/100 g versus roughly 3.8 g/100 g for couscous.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Quinoa, around 2.8 g/100 g compared with roughly 1.4 g/100 g for refined couscous.

faq.question: Does couscous contain gluten?
faq.answer: Yes. Traditional couscous is made from durum wheat.
